page: Microsoft Azure D8ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, alongside a 472 GB local NVMe SSD. The CPU architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations.

In benchmark evaluations, the D8ds_v6 demonstrates strong single-core performance, scoring 2171.0 in Geekbench single-core tests and achieving a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.31 GB/sec. Multi-core and memory performance generally align with the average tier, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 8331.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 14282.05. Memory bandwidth reaches 621.3 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 66.9 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, the system exhibits performance limitations on larger workloads, as evidenced by a weak text generation speed of 8.03 tokens/sec during medium (7B) LLM inference.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D8ds_v6 offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads, combining dedicated compute resources with high-speed local NVMe storage without the overhead of a dedicated GPU. This hardware profile is well-suited for applications requiring a balance of CPU and memory, such as relational databases, web serving, software compilation, and moderate text processing tasks.
